runs.description: Small-area face-channel equilibration pilot

params.scope: Representative K=3 late-window readouts from the finite-area quantum pilot. The regular input covers L=4,5,6 at U=0,1,5; a phase-shifted U=5 control shows preparation dependence. The study asks how readouts approach the exact dephased reference, not whether a canonical state is reached.
params.limits: Finite K=2,3 sectors, uniform complete-graph hopping with fixed row sum, two FL phase choices, three interaction strengths, and selected windows ending at t=200. Residence depends on the readout tolerance and observation window; phase-shifted cases are not energy matched. No large-area equilibration claim.

runs.description: Classical rotor spreading and equilibrium comparison

params.scope: Grouped late-time summaries compare four ring sizes, three packet-energy scales and fixed-packet versus fixed-density preparation. At packet energy 10, the hot-pair fraction follows the microcanonical value 2/N and equilibrium-region residence is 87.2–90.4%. At packet energy 100, the hot pair retains 98.7–99.0% of local energy through t=2000.
params.limits: Classical I=1 nearest-neighbor rings, equal-and-opposite initial hot pair, three related orientation seeds, and finite observation windows. The fixed-density series raises the initial packet energy with N; N=8 cases overlap between preparations. Late-time trapping is not permanent localization, and no quantum rotor evolution is included.
params.calculationStatus: 72 production runs (63 unique preparations), 144 microcanonical chains, and ten full-duration half-step controls; verification records included

runs.description: Few-rotor transfer: planar bound and 3D controls

params.scope: Six representative planar-pair ratios sample the exact pendulum bound and its numerical check. Three-dimensional zero-angular-momentum controls use seed 1701 across a triangle, open four-rotor chain and four-rotor ring at seven couplings. The common chart parameter is initial packet energy divided by coupling; series keep rotor count, topology and preparation separate.
params.limits: The planar pair is aligned and has one initially resting rotor; its exact threshold is T0=4λ and its maximum is an all-time bound. The 3D controls instead start with an equal-and-opposite hot pair and summarize finite-time cold kinetic energy. Their preparations and conserved quantities differ; they do not establish thermalization. The figure bands use all three seeds, while this downloadable sample fixes seed 1701.
params.calculationStatus: 14 planar-pair runs and 63 three-dimensional runs; six half-step controls, a symmetric-triangle control, and scalar-ODE/conservation checks recorded

runs.description: Rotor coupling crossover and delayed release

params.scope: The dashboard plots 56 grouped three-seed cases at the primary late window, plus eight direct-coupling checks. The ratio scan spans N=8,16,32,64 and 14 packet-energy-to-coupling ratios; separate direct controls vary λ at fixed packet energy and physical observation time.
params.limits: Three related orientation seeds and one equal-and-opposite hot-pair preparation. Significant/suppressed thresholds and the post-inspection half-response bracket are finite-grid diagnostics, not phase-transition estimates. Longer trajectories show delayed transfer, but release timing is step-sensitive; neither permanent localization nor universal equilibration is established.
params.calculationStatus: 168 primary trajectories plus 29 follow-up histories; 409 window summaries; finite-time brackets and delayed-transfer checks recorded

runs.description: Large-area tetrahedron: face activation and recurrence

params.scope: Exact FL free-hopping control on five/six channels, with four initial tetrahedral spinors and vacuum extras. Twenty controls span K=2..10000 and two phase choices. A fifth channel can take 29.06% of area, while individual areas and local energies recur.
params.limits: Unit complete-graph hopping, U=0, pure FL manifold. Direct sparse occupation evolution verifies K=1,2. No irreversible equipartition or interacting thermalization established. The two extra symmetric six-channel rows have the same normal, leaving only five distinct classical directions. Phase controls have different conserved initial energies.

runs.description: Entanglement of separately closed thermal polyhedra

params.scope: 86 temperatures over T*=0.05..5. Exact Schmidt eigenvalues and multiplicities yield entropy, area-sector decomposition, purity, Renyi-2 entropy and coherent joint singlet creation. Within-area entanglement exceeds area-distribution entropy at T*=1,2,5.
params.limits: Normalized double-singlet projection of the area-one F12 reference; initially only two active faces. Ordinary left/right tensor factorization. Adaptive area cutoffs 12..140; entropy truncation estimate below 6.4e-12 nats. Temperature slopes are prepared-state responses; fixed single-copy Gibbs and AdS interpretations are not assumed. General four-face FL inputs remain open.

runs.description: Candidate geometric Hamiltonians and prepared-FL dynamics

params.scope: Exact K=4, total-spin-zero study (dimension 105). The baseline is complete-graph face-to-face area exchange plus on-site repulsion, with equal hopping strength on each bond. We added the positive RS-volume term and the signed triple-grasp term as separate candidate Hamiltonians, then evolved five explicitly prepared FL references under the baseline and both signed couplings. The 62 parameter settings cover U/t=0,1,5,20 and normalized coupling alpha=-2,-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1,2; the ring is included only as a sparse-hopping control. The study contains 6,510 saved energy levels and 50 prepared-state trajectories.
params.limits: The complete graph represents tetrahedral face adjacency; the ring is a hopping control, not a proposed tetrahedron. The positive-volume and signed-grasp additions are tested candidate models, not derived physical interactions. Results use one copy, fixed K=4, project-normalized volume, and t=1; no physical coupling calibration or phase-transition claim is implied. The long-time dynamics are exact energy-basis samples with adaptive logarithmic coverage, not a uniformly resolved trace of every fast oscillation. Large thermal and dynamics CSVs are gzip-compressed for download; their source and package checksums are both listed.
params.calculationStatus: 62 Hamiltonian parameter settings and 50 FL trajectories calculated; 1,510 independent checks passed (maximum residual 1.07e-12)

runs.description: Four-site Hamiltonian spectra and RS-volume observables

params.scope: Exact diagonalization of the hopping-plus-on-site-repulsion operator H_G=-t Σ_(i,j)∈E_G(E_ij+E_ji)+(U/2)Σ_i n_i(n_i−1), where E_ij=a_i†a_j+b_i†b_j and n_i=a_i†a_i+b_i†b_i. Four sites, fixed boson number 2K and total spin zero; K=2,3,4 gives dimensions 20,50,105, with empty sites allowed. Compare the complete graph (6 hopping bonds) and periodic ring (4), with equal t per bond. The 30 cases use (t,U)=(0,1) or t=1 and U/t=0,1,5,20.
params.limits: The positive Rovelli–Smolin (RS) volume V=(γℏ)^(3/2)Σ_(connected triples)√|q_ijk|, q_ijk=i[J_i·J_j,J_j·J_k], is a separate observable evaluated on energy eigenstates and Gibbs states; it is not a term in H_G, and no g_V V coupling was calculated. The optional spin-exchange setting is g=0. Both graphs select the same four connected triples, so V is the same operator and only the hopping graph changes. Project-normalized volume; physical calibration is open. The temperature response is a finite-sector crossover, not a phase transition. Ground-state entropy uses the Gibbs mixture when degenerate.

volumeShape.title: Positive volume vs. tetrahedron shape
volumeShape.shapeScope: Equal face-area ratios only; this is a controlled subfamily at fixed total J, not all Gr(2,4) labels or all area partitions. Face labels are ordered and samples are not quotiented by leg permutations.

coordinates.phiRadians: Bending angle between the (0,1) and (2,3) face-normal planes
coordinates.crossRatio: lambda = <0,2><1,3> / (<0,3><1,2>) for the four normalized spinor rays
coordinates.thurstonRelation: For four marked points, lambda is a complex coordinate on M_0,4. It labels the spinor-ray configuration here; the cone-metric Kähler metric and its curvature data are not assumed to equal the LQG flux geometry.

volumeLabelEnumeration.title: Discrete quantum spin and recoupling labels at fixed total J
volumeLabelEnumeration.interpretation: Finite labelled SU(2) spin sectors and intertwiner channels; not a finite enumeration of classical coherent shapes.

t1b.title: Real-plane signed mean and positive-volume comparison
t1b.validation: Independent local-spin tensor-product check of the triple-grasp matrices and positive RS/AL expectations.

t5c.title: Input-geometry volume and flux-correlation comparison
t5c.definition: The input closed tetrahedron is the classical target. Weighted spinors encode its face areas and normals; G_ij = <J_i · J_j> and its normalized correlations are a separate shape-recovery diagnostic.
t5c.volumeScope: Legacy covariance geometry for 14 equal-area labels at J=1..6; new weighted input-volume scans for regular and unequal-skew shapes through J=7, a 9-point unequal-area grid at J=2,4, selected J=6 points, and a fixed-area flat path.
t5c.limitations: Finite exploratory scans; neither large-J convergence nor either order of the degenerate and large-J limits is established. Individual flux-vector means vanish in the gauge-invariant FL state. Under the tested 4-valent signs, calibrated RS/AL curves coincide by closure and are not independent evidence.
t5c.normalization: Project units include gamma^(3/2), gamma=0.2375, hbar=1. Fixed geometry factors are sqrt(2)/12 (RS) and sqrt(2)/6 (AL); AL uses lexicographic signs (+1,-1,+1,-1).
